name: Hugo
tagline: The Go-powered static site generator built for build speed

seo.title: Hugo: Overview, Strengths, and Trade-offs
seo.description: What Hugo is, why its build times are still unmatched, and where its template language becomes the limiting factor on larger projects.

intro:
Hugo is a static site generator written in Go, distributed as a single binary with no runtime dependencies. Its defining characteristic is build speed: sites with tens of thousands of pages rebuild in under a second, because it parallelizes across all available cores and caches aggressively between runs. Content lives in Markdown with frontmatter, and structure comes from a directory convention rather than configuration.

Templates are written in Go's html/template syntax plus a set of Hugo-specific functions. That language is fast and predictable, but it is not a general-purpose programming language, and complex conditional layouts tend to turn into nested with and if blocks that are hard to refactor. Hugo has no component model and no client-side interactivity story; if you need a dropdown that updates state, you are adding a separate script by hand. This is a reference entry used by the comparison pages.
